title.en: Eco on writing and The Name of the Rose

heading.en: A serious novel that sold millions

hook.en: Publishers often say readers want only light books. Yet a long, difficult novel about a medieval monastery became a worldwide best-seller. How?

objectives.en: Explain Eco's narrative style in academic writing
Describe The Name of the Rose and its surprising success
Recognise the features of the interview as a form

narration.en: Publishers often say readers want only light books. Yet a long, difficult novel about a medieval monastery became a worldwide best-seller. How?

body.en: Eco says his scholarly writing is unusual because it has a narrative quality: he tells the story of his research, including his trials and errors, instead of just presenting conclusions. This playful, story-like approach comes from his love of narration, which he later expressed fully in his novels.

points.en: Scholarly work written in a narrative style

Includes trials and errors, not just conclusions

say.en: At the centre is Eco's best-known novel, The Name of the Rose.
On the surface it is a detective story with a mystery to solve.
Underneath, it explores metaphysics, the big questions of being.
It deals with theology and religious debate.
It is set in the medieval world and is rich in history.
It sold millions of copies around the world.
Eco believes timing was part of the mystery of its success.

body.en: The Name of the Rose is a serious novel that works as a detective story but also explores metaphysics, theology and medieval history. Eco finds its huge success something of a mystery. He suggests that readers do not only want easy books; and he feels that if it had been written ten years earlier or later, it might not have succeeded in the same way. Timing played a part.

points.en: A detective story with philosophy, theology and history
Timing helped: success is partly a mystery

problem.en: What reasons does Eco suggest for the success of The Name of the Rose?

steps.en: Say he finds the success partly a mystery.
Give the reason about readers: they do not want only easy reading.
Give the reason about timing: a different decade might have changed the result.

answer.en: Eco calls its success a mystery. He suggests that readers also enjoy challenging books, not only easy ones, and that timing mattered: written ten years earlier or later, it might not have succeeded the same way.
